claim: The system serves tourists, DOT tourism administrators, and DOT-accredited establishments, and was developed using Laravel, PostgreSQL, and Bootstrap 5 with JavaScript.
The rapid advancement of digital technology has significantly transformed the tourism industry by changing how travelers access information, plan trips, and select destinations [1].
Current travelers increasingly depend on digital platforms to search for tourist attractions, accommodations, transportation options, restaurants, and other travel-related information [2].

Through the integration of digital transformation, artificial intelligence, recommendation systems, and tourism analytics, these platforms enable tourism organizations to deliver personalized services, improve access to reliable tourism information, and support data-driven decision-making processes [3], [4], [5].
In a global context, TripAdvisor is one of the platforms that provides tourists with information and recommendations on destinations, accommodations, restaurants, and travel experiences [6].
In the Philippines, the Department of Tourism (DOT) promotes tourism destinations across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao through its official tourism platforms and initiatives [7].

The Department of Tourism (DOT) Region XI is the lead government agency responsible for tourism promotion, regulation, enterprise development, accreditation of tourism establishments, and implementation of tourism-related policies in the Davao Region [8].
These technologies serve as tools for improving tourism services and strengthening destination competitiveness through technology-driven approaches [9], [10].

Without an integrated system that monitors tourist behavior, tourist volume, and destination preferences, the agency is limited in its ability to generate the analytical insights needed to develop and promote tourism in Region XI [11].
Intelligent technologies have been successfully applied in tourism recommendation systems using various recommendation approaches [12], [13].

Among these approaches, Content-Based Recommendation has been utilized to provide personalized destination recommendations by matching destination features with tourists’ selected or expressed preferences [14].
Intelligent algorithms, user preference analysis, and decision-support techniques have also helped tourists make destination choices and plan trips more effectively [12], [13].
This enables tourism systems to recommend destinations and related services based on tourists’ travel patterns [15].
Aside from improving recommendation quality, these patterns also provide tourism organizations with insights into user behavior and relationships among destination entities [15].

Recent developments in intelligent recommendation systems have also improved the ability of smart tourism platforms to generate convenient travel plans from recommended tourist attractions [16], [17], [18].
This feature improves tourist convenience by reducing the effort required to plan complex multi-destination trips [17], [18].
Limited support is available for accreditation verification, tourism analytics, tracking tourist behavior, and intelligent decision support for tourism administrators [12], [19].

Other smart tourism applications also tend to operate as standalone systems that provide only selected intelligent features instead of integrating multiple smart technologies into one centralized tourism platform [16], [19].

Likewise, tourism administrators need tourism data and behavioral insights to support destination promotion, policy development, tourism infrastructure planning, and evidence-based decision-making [10], [11].

A centralized intelligent tourism platform can help address these needs by improving access to tourism data, strengthening tourism governance, and enhancing the tourist experience in the region [12], [13].
The system uses the Content-Based Recommendation method to match each tourist’s profile and preferences with the attributes of tourism destinations [14].

It also applies Association Rule Mining through the Apriori Algorithm to identify relationships among destinations, hotels, restaurants, and souvenir shops based on historical tourist visitation records [15].
In addition, the system supports map-based navigation services to help tourists locate selected destinations and tourism establishments through mapping technologies [20].
Table 1 presents the comparison of ExploreDVO with existing tourism platforms, namely TripAdvisor (A), the DOT Philippines Travel Website (B), and the DOT Facebook Page (C).

The study supports Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure by utilizing digital technologies to improve tourism services and aligns with the University of Mindanao's research agenda on Information and Communication Technology (ICT) innovations and digital transformation.

Developed with Laravel, PostgreSQL, and Bootstrap 5 with JavaScript, the platform aims to enable tourists to conveniently access DOT-accredited destinations, accommodations, restaurants, and souvenir shops through a responsive, user-friendly interface.

2.2.1.1 The system shall require tourism administrators and DOT-accredited tourism establishments to register their names, email addresses, passwords, contact information, and other necessary details to create an account.
Tourists are not required to register or create an account to use the system; an account is entirely optional (see Section 2.2.3.1.1).

2.2.1.2 The system shall require registered tourism administrators and DOT-accredited tourism establishments to log in using their credentials to access the system based on their assigned roles and permissions.

2.2.1.3 Tourist users shall be able to browse DOT-accredited tourism destinations, accommodations, restaurants, souvenir establishments, tour packages, and other tourism-related information within the Davao Region.

2.2.1.4 Tourist users shall receive personalized destination recommendations based on their travel preferences, including travel purpose, visitor type, budget, accommodation preference, duration of stay, distance, health conditions, ratings, and interests, using the Content-Based Recommendation technique.
2.2.1.5 Tourist users shall be able to generate AI-driven travel itineraries based on their selected travel preferences, recommended destinations, travel duration, budget, and destination proximity.

2.2.1.6 Tourist users shall have access to GPS-based navigation through Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap to assist them in locating selected tourism destinations and DOT-accredited tourism establishments.
2.2.1.7 Tourist users shall be able to submit ratings, reviews, and exit survey responses regarding their tourism experiences and visited establishments.

2.2.1.8 Tourism administrators shall be able to manage DOT-accredited tourism destinations, accommodations, restaurants, souvenir establishments, tour packages, and other tourism-related information within the platform.
2.2.1.9 Tourism administrators shall be able to verify and monitor the accreditation status of tourism establishments and maintain updated accreditation records.

2.2.1.10 Tourism administrators shall be able to generate tourism analytics, tourist behavior analyses, data visualization dashboards, and date-filtered reports to support tourism planning, monitoring, and decision-making.
2.2.1.11 DOT-accredited tourism establishments shall be able to update and maintain their establishment information, services, facilities, and tourism-related content within the system.

2.2.1.12 The system shall generate association-based recommendations by identifying relationships among tourism destinations, accommodations, restaurants, souvenir establishments, and tour packages using Association Rule Mining through the Apriori Algorithm based on historical tourist visitation records collected through exit survey responses.
2.2.1.13 The system shall provide chatbot assistance through a chatbot API to respond to tourism-related inquiries and assist users in exploring tourism information.

2.2.1.14 Tourist users shall be able to optionally provide health or accessibility information, subject to explicit consent, to receive destination suitability guidance in compliance with RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012).

2.2.1.15 Tourism administrators shall be able to post advisories, either platform-wide or for a specific listing, to notify travelers of temporary conditions such as closures, restrictions, or safety notices.

2.2.1.16 Tourist users shall be able to adopt a DOT-accredited tour operator's published, ready-made package itinerary as their travel plan directly, as an alternative to generating one through the Content-Based Recommendation and AI-Driven Itinerary Generation pipeline.

2.2.1.17 Tourist users shall be able to swap any stop of a generated itinerary for one of the most similar available places, ranked by a pretrained text-embedding model, and shall be offered the closest open substitute when a planned place is unavailable on their travel dates.
2.2.1.18 The system shall not recommend a place that is closed on the tourist’s travel dates.

2.2.1.19 The system shall group the stops of a generated itinerary into days so that the places sharing a day are alike, using a pretrained text-embedding model, without adding or removing any stop and without increasing the total travelling by more than a set limit.

2.2.1.20 The system shall automatically delete anonymous itineraries, trip preferences and chatbot questions after a fixed retention period, so that data about an anonymous visitor is not kept longer than its purpose requires, in line with RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012).

2.2.1.21 The system shall warn tourism administrators when accreditations are about to expire or have expired, and shall hide an establishment with an expired accreditation from tourists until it is renewed.

2.2.1.22 The system shall record every sign-in, failed sign-in and change made by a tourism administrator in an audit log that administrators can review, without recording passwords or the contents typed into forms.

2.2.1.23 The system shall limit how often a visitor can sign in, register, build a trip or save places within a given time, and shall keep daily backups of its data, including a copy stored away from the server.

2.2.1.24 The system shall match a tourist’s picked interests to places by meaning, using the same pretrained text-embedding model, and shall fall back to keyword matching when the stored vectors are unavailable.

2.2.1.25 The system shall keep every visit of a generated itinerary inside the place’s opening hours and open days where these are known, shall limit the time a day may spend driving, and shall choose one stay for the trip that is not an hours-long drive from the stops of any day.

2.2.1.26 The chatbot shall answer a question about a named place from the listing’s own data (where it is, what it costs, its hours, and whether it is open and DOT-accredited) and shall not recommend a place that is closed or not accredited.

2.2.1.27 The system shall let a tourist optionally enter a departure date, time and point, and shall plan the last day of the itinerary so that the estimated journey to that point is completed with an allowance before the departure.

2.2.1.28 The system shall choose the accommodation for each night of a multi-day trip, shall avoid changing accommodation unless the trip is Remote or the nights cannot otherwise be covered, and shall tell the tourist when no accredited accommodation could be used for a night.
2.2.1.29 The system shall label listings, accreditation records, exit surveys and association rules that are sample or simulated data, so that they are not mistaken for DOT-verified records.
2.2.1.30 The system shall let a tourist rate the service and the amenities of a listing in addition to the overall rating, and shall let the establishment reply to a review.

2.2.1.31 The system shall offer an optional AI-assisted grouping of the planner’s stops into days that is advisory only and is discarded whenever its answer is invalid or does not give a plan that is at least as feasible as the planner’s own.
2.2.1.32 The system shall let a partner establishment submit a tour package for review by the tourism administrator, and shall record each step of the review.

A full copy of the database and the uploaded files is made automatically every night and kept for 14 days on the server, and an additional copy is made before every software update (the latest 10 of these are kept).

Each interest is described by one short sentence, which the same pretrained model (nomic-embed-text) turns into a vector of 768 numbers.

When a tourist picks interests, their vectors are averaged, and every candidate destination is scored by the cosine similarity (Equation 10) between its own vector and that average, rescaled so that the best match among the candidates is 1 and the worst is 0.

This interest fit is applied first when the destinations are ranked: places that fit the picked interests come before those that do not, and the Destination Recommendation Score (Equation 3) orders the places within each group.

The schedule builder works as a clock simulation: it starts at the tourist’s arrival time on the first day and at breakfast (7:00 AM) on every later day, and each stop pushes the clock forward by its journey and its visit (150 minutes, or 90 where the day has to fit more in).

Meals drop in when the clock reaches their window: lunch around 12:00 noon, moved within a window of 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM, dinner at about 6:30 PM (it may start between 6:00 PM and 7:30 PM), overnight at 8:00 PM; a meal that would fall outside its window is skipped instead of invented.
A day’s sightseeing has to finish by 6:00 PM, and a stop that cannot is moved to the next day.
A tourist who lands before 6:00 AM first gets a rest, freshen-up and breakfast block at the accommodation, and the first outing starts at 8:00 AM as on every other day.
A tourist who would reach the accommodation after 7:30 PM, the end of the dinner window, is given only a late check-in and overnight stay, because a dinner would otherwise fall after midnight.

Where a destination’s hours are a plain daily schedule, such as 8:00 AM–5:00 PM or a morning and an afternoon session, a visit waits for opening for at most an hour, is cut short to end at closing time, and a place that opens later in the day is visited after the morning stop; a place that closes before anyone could reach it is skipped without blocking the rest of the day.

Hours may also name days, such as Mon–Sat 8:00 AM–5:00 PM or Closed Mondays: the planner works out the date of each day of the trip from the start date and does not schedule a place on a weekday it is closed, moving it to another day when it can.

A day may also spend only a limited time on the road, counted on the slow end of the travel estimates and including the journey back to where the day ends: 3.5 hours for a Close Proximity preference, 5 hours for Commutable and 7 hours for Remote.
At the end of the trip a souvenir shop is added only when one lies within 20 km of the last stop and the visit can end by 7:00 PM.

Night n is spent between the last stop of day n and the first stop of day n + 1, so a stay costs the estimated journey from the one plus the journey to the other, estimated in the same way as every journey in the schedule (the detour factor, the Samal ferry, and the tourist’s way of getting around).
Changing stay carries a penalty of 30 minutes on a Remote trip, and the plan with the smallest total of journeys and changes is chosen.

A stay suggested by an association rule replaces the stay of a block of nights only when it is eligible on all of those nights and adds no more than 15 minutes of travelling in total, so the association rule can choose between stays that are about equally good but never creates a change of stay, and a stay more than 60 km from any stop of the trip is passed over.

When these are given, the last day is planned so that the journey from the last stop to the departure point, which is the planner’s own estimate (straight-line distance multiplied by 1.3 for detours, at the slowest pace, without a routing service), still arrives at least 120 minutes before the departure time.

The 120 minutes is a planning allowance stated on the itinerary and not an airline or airport rule, since check-in and security needs differ by carrier and route, and it can be changed in the system configuration.
Closed places remain visible on their own pages with a notice such as “Temporarily closed until December 1,” so a tourist can see why a place is missing.

The system relies on the status entered by DOT and the establishments; it does not detect a closure on its own, and opening days and hours are used only where they are written in a form the system can read, such as 8:00 AM–5:00 PM or Mon–Sat 8:00 AM–5:00 PM, and they must be entered by DOT, which manages the destination listings.

In addition, because most official accommodation records expired on 31 October 2026 and DOT’s renewals are pending, a test grace date of 31 December 2026, set in the system configuration, keeps those stays available while the system is being tested; it is a testing setting and not an accreditation decision, and it is to be removed once DOT confirms the renewals.
